model.feasible_actions: one unit-effort assignment to either agent for the task's skill
model.production_timing: evaluate at D_t, then update D_next=D_t+1 for the assigned agent-skill
model.reward_unit: productivity/output units per one-unit task; assumed calibrated
simplifications: one task per period; each type requires exactly one corresponding skill
unit effort and unit experience increment; no shared cross-task resource coupling
skills and agent-skill experience cells evolve independently
reward is task-skill output, with no CES, threshold, costs, teaching, noise, or switching cost

scientific_interpretation: No positive dynamic-versus-best-static case was observed in this design. The tested model has independent skill-specific experience and reward, so this result is consistent with the discrete-convexity argument in the protocol.
status: small deterministic parameter study; not a campaign

structural_check.claim: For each skill, cumulative reward F_i(n)=sum_{m=0}^{n-1}P_i(D0_i+m) has increasing discrete increments. Thus F_0(n0)+F_1(n-n0) is convex in n0 and its maximum occurs at an endpoint; with no cross-skill or shared-resource coupling, assigning every occurrence of a task type to one agent is at least as good as splitting it dynamically.
structural_check.classification: mathematical deduction from the specified model
structural_check.scope: applies only to the declared independent-skill, linear-output, unit-task model; it does not establish a result for coupled tasks or shared period capacities
